objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026), idea 1 of its reply to John's 'What do you think we could build out of something like this?': under the parity law with the cheapest counts (the policy of TOUCH-CENSUS-20261118-001 and RING-GROWTH-20261118-001), when a ring of knots with spare distinctions (exponential growth) is joined to a two-fold-growing piece (two touching knots) by one shared distinction, a shared knot or a short path of knots, does each part keep its own growth, does one take over, or does something new appear? Which is typical across the small ways of joining them, and do two joined rings add, multiply or lock their rates? Junction counts by round, long horizon, exact linear recurrences. Serves G17 (and G2). Stop at a rule for how growth series combine under joins, or a counterexample family.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Successful, 9 of 10 frozen predictions held; referee pending): under the cheapest counts, trees of knots joined to a ring compose as independent factors of one return equation y^n (1+y)^j prod F = 1, F_s = 1 + y(1+y)^s per joined knot (exact on 27 single-ring tests and all 48 census joins by a shared distinction or knot); the ring takes over and every tree join speeds it; one chord closes the start; two joined rings grow non-rationally, c ~ C lambda^t t^(-3/2), lambda 2.14 to 2.79; post hoc, menus nest along chains.
stop_rule: One pilot (fitting), one frozen census of joins, read-out, referee hand-off, report.
title: Do growth behaviours compose when growing parts are joined?
